Subject: Re: Performance protections — MedEdge request

Hi Soojin / Ben,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal pushed back on standard credits as the sole remedy for repeat production-impacting latency. They asked us to put a concrete commercial mechanism on the table that gives them an exit / cash remedy for chronic outages rather than just service credits.

Their high-level asks:
- Termination right for MedEdge if we breach a P1 latency target (p99 response > 1.2s) in 3 of any rolling 60-day windows.
- Fee-at-risk / escrowed reserve equal to 4x monthly committed spend (to be returned pro rata if we cure).
- Liquidated damages cap: per-incident payment equal to 1x monthly committed spend (cumulative uncapped up to escrow).

They attached an initial term sketch (MEDEDGE_initial_ask.pdf). Priya from Legal is copied and available for redlines.

From our perspective, the ask is material and changes how we price / underwrite the account. Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept any of these structures (even in a constrained form)? If not, we need a clean explanation and a counter.

Happy to hop on a short call today if helpful.

Best,
Alex

Subject: Re: Performance protections — MedEdge request

Alex, thanks for the note and the term sketch — got it. We appreciate the candor; I want to be explicit about constraints so we can converge quickly.

Short answers up front:
- A straightforward, uncapped termination right tied to 3 P1 misses in 60 days is unlikely without a material commercial offset.
- Escrowed reserves / fee-at-risk constructs may be possible if we bound the exposure and tie drawdown mechanics to a clear cure plan and RCA window.
- Liquidated damages as a simple per-incident cash payment are something we can consider if capped and tied to measurable, objective criteria (e.g., sustained p99 > 1.2s for > 4 hours AND customer-impact confirmed).

Request from our side to make a workable counterproposal:
1) Define P1 precisely (customer-visible latency affecting >=10% of Production traces for > 5 minutes OR p99 > 1.2s sustained for > 4 hours).
2) Propose a capped escrow equal to 2 months committed spend (we can consider increasing to 3 months with additional contractual concessions).
3) Stepwise cure timeline: immediate remediation window + 30-day engineering plan; escalation to dedicated runbook and prioritized capacity within 14 days of confirmed P1.
4) Termination right limited to unresolved condition persisting 60 days after confirmed P1 (i.e., not immediate termination on first incident).

I've attached a short excerpt from our SLA playbook that explains standard cure/rollback behavior and some examples (SLA_playbook_excerpt.pdf).

Ben/Vanessa — can you review and confirm whether 2 months escrow + the stepwise cure/60d termination ceiling is something we can present? If legal wants to see specific phrasing, Priya — feel free to suggest redline points.

If MedEdge wants to push for more (e.g., 4 months escrow), we should ask for either higher committed/discounted pricing or an operational commitment (e.g., dedicated capacity pool for MedEdge).

I can take a 30-minute call today at 4pm PT to work through.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: SLA_playbook_excerpt.pdf]

Thanks, Soojin. The MedEdge team discussed your counter internally. A few points back from procurement/legal:
- They will accept a reduction of escrow to 3 months if we sign a 12-month committed purchase order (volume guarantee).
- They need a clearer drawdown mechanism: automatic partial drawdown if SLA not met after 14 days post-confirmation, full drawdown after 60 days unresolved.
- Termination: they will accept the 60-day cure ladder only if there is a contractual step that allows pro rata repayment of escrow if remediation is demonstrated within a subsequent 30-day window.

Separately, Priya asked if you could share a redline-friendly doc. She prefers to see language rather than bullets. We can share our legal contact info for a quick exchange.

On the LD cap: they want per-incident LD = 1x monthly committed spend but willing to cap cumulative payable liability at 4x monthly spend (which they claim is lower than their previous ask of uncapped).

Would Redwood be able to accept: 3 months escrow (with 12-mo commitment), partial drawdown ladder, cumulative cap 4x monthly, and 60-day cure with pro rata return on remediation?

-Alex

Alex / Priya — thanks for the clear counter. I ran this with Product, CS, Finance and Legal; below is a pragmatic counterproposal Redwood can present to MedEdge legal that narrows risk while being commercially meaningful. Please note this is a commercial summary — Legal will draft final language.

Redwood counter (high level):
1) Escrowed reserve: 2 months committed spend on execution. With a 12-month minimum commitment and modest price uplift (+10%), Redwood will expand escrow to 3 months.
2) Drawdown mechanics: Limited automatic drawdown after 21 days from confirmed P1 if no material remediation, partial drawdown tied to measurable SLA windows; full drawdown only after 60 days unresolved. Any drawdown reduces escrow pro rata; remaining escrow refundable upon remediation per agreed schedule.
3) Liquidated damages: Per-incident LD payable if (a) p99 > 1.2s sustained for > 4 hours AND (b) MedEdge impact threshold met. LD = 0.75x monthly committed spend per qualifying incident. Cumulative LD payable capped at the escrow amount (not uncapped).
4) Termination: MedEdge may initiate termination only after two qualifying P1 events within any rolling 90-day period AND failure to remediate within 60 days of the second confirmed P1. Immediate termination on single event is not permitted.
5) Operational commitments: Redwood will provide a joint RCA within 7 business days of a confirmed P1 and prioritize incident post-mortem for a permanent mitigation plan. If MedEdge opts for Dedicated capacity, Redwood will extend a 30% performance credit for the first 3 months to offset migration impact.

Next steps:
- If MedEdge accepts the commercial summary above, Legal teams can convert to redline language.
- Vanessa and Marissa — please schedule a 45-min legal + procurement sync with MedEdge next week and attach the counterproposal doc (counterproposal_term_ctrt_v2.docx).

Alex — can you confirm whether MedEdge can accept capped LD at 0.75x monthly and the two-event termination floor? If they insist on the 4x cumulative cap, we will need either higher uplift or a dedicated capacity commitment.

Thanks all — I’ll be on the call next Wed 9am PT if that works.

Best,
Soojin Lee
